question: How many development and welfare related subjects have been transferred from the state to the Panchayati Raj Institution through constitutional amendments in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is **29**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The "Panchayats" Part IX, containing the provisions of **Articles 243 to 243(O)**, and the "Eleventh Schedule," containing 29 subjects relating to Panchayat activities, were both included by the 73rd Amendment in 1992.
 
• **Article 40** of the DPSP, states that "The State shall take steps to organize Gram Panchayats and confer on them such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government."
 
• This amendment has elevated Gram Panchayats from a **non-justiciable** part of the Constitution to a justiciable part of the Constitution, and it has given the states a constitutional obligation to enact Panchayati Raj Acts, however, considering their unique there is enough freedom. Geographical, political-administrative, and other circumstances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Unlike urban and suburban municipalities, Panchayati Raj is a system of local self-government for villages in rural India.
 
• It includes **Panchayati Raj institutions**, which enable the attainment of rural self-governance.
 
• It includes Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), which enable villages to practice **self-governance**.
 
• Their mandate is to "strengthen social justice, advance economic development, and implement Central and State Government schemes, including the **29** issues enumerated in the Eleventh Schedule."
